'''Liang Sili''' ({{zh|s=梁思礼|t=梁思禮}}; 24 August 1924 – 14 April 2016) was a Chinese aerospace engineer. He was elected an academician of the [[International Academy of Astronautics]] in 1987 and the [[Chinese Academy of Sciences]] in 1993. He became the vice-president of the [[International Astronautical Federation]] in 1994.

Liang was the youngest son of Chinese scholar and reformist [[Liang Qichao]].<ref>{{cite news|title=梁思礼回忆在津度过的17年：人生从饮冰室开始|url=http://news.sohu.com/20070422/n249608632.shtml|access-date=15 April 2016|publisher=Sohu|date=22 April 2007|language=Chinese}}</ref> His elder brothers, [[Liang Sicheng]] and [[Liang Siyong]], were also academicians.<ref>{{cite news|title=梁家有方三院士：梁思成、梁思永、梁思礼|url=http://news.sciencenet.cn/htmlnews/2014/8/301208.shtm|access-date=15 April 2016|publisher=Chinese Science News|date=15 August 2014|language=Chinese}}</ref>

==Education==
Liang started his [[Undergraduate education|undergraduate studies]] at [[Carleton College]] in the United States in 1941. He transferred to [[Purdue University]] in 1943 and graduated from there with a bachelor's degree with a major in [[electrical engineering]] in 1945. He received a doctor of philosophy in [[Automation|missile control]] from the [[University of Cincinnati]] in 1949.<ref>{{Cite web |title=梁思礼院士----2016 |url=http://casad.cas.cn/zt_124343/mhys/2016/201604/t20160420_4683103.html |access-date=2023-03-05 |website=casad.cas.cn}}</ref>

== Career ==
Liang returned to China in late 1949 when the [[Chinese Communist Party]] took control of mainland China. He was appointed jobs at the Institute of Telecommunications Technology (Ministry of Posts & Telecommunications) and later the Institute of Electronic Science (Communication Department of PLA). In 1956, Liang transferred to the Fifth Institute of Ministry of Defense. He became the deputy director of the Research Office of Missile Control Systems, working under [[Qian Xuesen]].<ref name="Fifth Institute">{{cite news|title=梁思礼：苍穹大业赤子心|url=http://www.qstheory.cn/science/2015-12/18/c_1117508301.htm|access-date=15 April 2016|publisher=Qiushi|date=18 December 2015|language=Chinese|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160423001300/http://www.qstheory.cn/science/2015-12/18/c_1117508301.htm|archive-date=23 April 2016|url-status=dead}}</ref> Liang played an important role in the design of the [[Dongfeng (missile)#Dongfeng 2 (CSS-1)|Dongfeng 2A missile]], the [[DF-5|Dongfeng 5 missile]], the [[Long March 2 (rocket family)|Long March 2 rocket]], and the [[Long March 3|Long March 3 rocket]].<ref name="Fifth Institute" />

Liang died on 14 April 2016, at the age of 91, in [[Beijing]].<ref>{{cite news|title=梁启超之子中国火箭与导弹控制系统专家梁思礼逝世|url=http://mil.news.sina.com.cn/china/2016-04-15/doc-ifxriqqx2478622.shtml|access-date=15 April 2016|publisher=Sina|date=15 April 2016|language=Chinese}}</ref>
